problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}2a-b=7 \\ \frac{a}{5}-\frac{2b}{5}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution to the system of equations given above.

$a=$
{{field-1}}$,\,b=$
{{field-2}}
worked_solution:
To get rid of the fractions in the second equation, we must multiply the second equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $5.$

$$
{\begin{aligned}2a-b=7 \\ \frac{a}{5}-\frac{2b}{5}=1 & |\,\times 5\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}2a-b=7 \\ a-2b=5\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Let's solve for $a$ in the second equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}a-2b & =5 \\ a & =5+2b\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can substitute $a=5+2b$ into the first equation and solve for $b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2a-b & =7 \\ 2(5+2b)-b & =7 \\ 10+4b-b & =7 \\ 3b & =-3 \\ b & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of $a,$ we substitute $b=-1$ into the equation $a=5+2b,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =5+2b \\  & =5+2(-1) \\  & =5-2 \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $a=3,\,b=-1.$
